title: Secret cult chapel behind a boarded panel that sinks into the floor
what: A secret room found by pushing a section of timber boarding: the panel (a block of floor raised to the ceiling, boarded like the wall around it) sinks into the floor and opens a low passage. The room behind is a timber-shored chapel with cobbled floor: a long desk-altar along one wall with candles, an open book and a skull, the Shadow Cloak on it, a wall cabinet, and a cultist. Walking into it counts the secret. The panel looks exactly like the wall around it; the hint is the frame of darker timber around it (inferred from tiles 170/171 around the panel, not seen in a frame).
recipe: Panel: sector 574, about 1024 x 256 units, kSectorZMotion (600), off_floor_z = ceiling (-49152, so it is a solid block), on_floor_z -20480 (floor of the passage), trigger_wall_push, busy 10, wait 30 (it rises again), retrigger; walls tile 170 wooden boarding and 171 to match the corridor; kGenSound (709) data 119/168 for the scrape. Passage 573 beyond, 1.7 bodies high (ceil -49152, floor -20480). Chapel 564: 13 x 9 m, 2.1 bodies high, floor tile 110 cobbles, ceiling 434; XSECTOR trigger_enter, trigger_once, tx 2 (kChannelSecretFound) cmd 64. Altar 466: sector raised 9216 (0.54 body) along the wall, 4 x kDecorationCandle (type 32, tile 938) with shades -128 / -27 / -14, kItemShadowCloak (type 113, tile 896), Tommy drum, sawed-off shells. A hanging lamp tile 641 over a corner, with concentric shade rings beneath it.
use: Behind the panelling of the saloon's back room, or of the theatre's green room: a cult chapel hidden in an ordinary building. Also a crypt side-chapel behind a sinking stone slab.
